final_message:
Fixed. The bug was in `render_invoice` in `billing/render.py`. It worked out the tax label and the inclusive flag, but then hit a leftover `pass` and never added a tax row to the output. I replaced the `pass` with code that adds the tax row. For tax-inclusive lines, the label gets " included" appended.

I also added your test as `tests/test_render_invoice.py` and wrote `answer.json` in the repository root. The full suite passes (25 tests).

steps.command: cd billing && cat render.py tax.py; ls

cd .. && python3 - <<'E'
p='billing/render.py'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace("        pass\n","        if inclusive:\n            label += \" included\"\n        out.append(_row(label, format_amount(invoice[\"tax_total\"], currency)))\n")
open(p,'w').write(s)
E
echo '{"file": "render.py", "function": "render_invoice"}' > answer.json
cat >> tests/test_render_invoice.py <<'E'
from billing.render import render_invoice


def test_render_invoice(world):
    from billing import tax

    tax.set_tax_rate(world.ctx, "US-CA", 825, "CA")
    cus = world.customer(region="US-CA")
    world.engine.subscribe(cus["id"], [(world.monthly["id"], 1)])
    [inv] = world.engine.invoices_for(cus["id"])
    text = render_invoice(world.ctx, inv)
    assert "Invoice INV-00001" in text
    assert "Tax (8.25%)" in text
    assert "$10.82" in text
E
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -5
